latest_nl_proof:
Let M_i = S/(g_1,...,g_i) for 0 <= i <= d, with M_0 = S. Since each g_i is homogeneous, each ideal (g_1,...,g_i) is homogeneous, so each M_i inherits a grading. Because all weights w_j are positive, the degree-n piece S_n is finite-dimensional over k: it has basis the monomials x_1^{a_1}...x_d^{a_d} with a_1 w_1 + ... + a_d w_d = n, and there are only finitely many such tuples. Hence every (M_i)_n is finite-dimensional as a quotient of S_n, so all Hilbert series below are well-defined.

First compute Hilb_S(q). The monomials form a k-basis of S, and deg(x_1^{a_1}...x_d^{a_d}) = a_1 w_1 + ... + a_d w_d. Therefore, as a formal power series,
Hilb_S(q) = sum_{a_1,...,a_d >= 0} q^{a_1 w_1 + ... + a_d w_d} = prod_{j=1}^d (sum_{m >= 0} q^{m w_j}) = 1 / prod_{j=1}^d (1 - q^{w_j}).
When d = 0, this is the empty product 1, which equals Hilb_k(q).

Now fix i with 1 <= i <= d, and let g_i_bar be the image of g_i in M_{i-1}. Because g_1,...,g_d is a regular sequence, g_i_bar is a non-zero-divisor on M_{i-1}. Let e_i = deg(g_i). Consider the shifted graded module M_{i-1}(-e_i), defined by M_{i-1}(-e_i)_n = (M_{i-1})_{n-e_i}. Multiplication by g_i_bar gives a degree-preserving map
M_{i-1}(-e_i) -> M_{i-1},   m |-> g_i_bar m.
It is injective because g_i_bar is a non-zero-divisor, and its cokernel is M_{i-1}/g_i_bar M_{i-1}, which is naturally isomorphic to S/(g_1,...,g_i) = M_i. Thus we have a short exact sequence of graded k-vector spaces
0 -> M_{i-1}(-e_i) -> M_{i-1} -> M_i -> 0.

Taking degree-n parts and dimensions, for every n we get
dim_k((M_i)_n) = dim_k((M_{i-1})_n) - dim_k((M_{i-1})_{n-e_i}),
where the last term is understood as 0 if n - e_i < 0. Summing over n >= 0 shows
Hilb_{M_i}(q) = Hilb_{M_{i-1}}(q) - q^{e_i} Hilb_{M_{i-1}}(q) = (1 - q^{e_i}) Hilb_{M_{i-1}}(q),
because by definition of the shift, Hilb_{M_{i-1}(-e_i)}(q) = q^{e_i} Hilb_{M_{i-1}}(q).

Iterating this identity for i = 1,2,...,d yields
Hilb_{S/(g_1,...,g_d)}(q) = Hilb_{M_d}(q) = Hilb_S(q) prod_{i=1}^d (1 - q^{e_i}) = (prod_{i=1}^d (1 - q^{e_i})) / (prod_{i=1}^d (1 - q^{w_i})).
This is exactly the claimed formula.
role_in_parent: Computes the quotient Hilbert series and identifies it with Q_{A,B,d}(q).
statement_nl: Let k be a field, let d be a nonnegative integer, let w_1,...,w_d be positive integers, and let S = k[x_1,...,x_d] be graded by deg(x_i)=w_i. If g_1,...,g_d is a homogeneous regular sequence in S and deg(g_i)=e_i for each i, then the graded Hilbert series of the quotient is Hilb_{S/(g_1,...,g_d)}(q) = prod_{i=1}^d (1 - q^(e_i)) / prod_{i=1}^d (1 - q^(w_i)).

domain_restrictions: Each w_i is a positive integer
S is graded by assigning deg(x_i)=w_i
Each g_i is homogeneous with respect to this grading
The sequence g_1,...,g_d is a regular sequence in S
The quotient is by the ideal generated by g_1 through g_d
Degrees e_i are the grading degrees of g_i; consistent with homogeneity (typically nonnegative in a weighted polynomial grading)
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: Given a weighted graded polynomial ring S equal to k[x_1,...,x_d] with deg(x_i)=w_i where k is a field, d is a nonnegative integer, and each w_i is a positive integer, suppose g_1,...,g_d is a homogeneous regular sequence in S such that deg(g_i)=e_i for each i. Then the graded Hilbert series of the quotient ring S modulo the ideal generated by g_1,...,g_d is equal to the product over i from 1 to d of (1 minus q to the e_i) divided by the product over i from 1 to d of (1 minus q to the w_i).
quantifier_order: Let d be a nonnegative integer
For all choices of positive integers w_1 through w_d
Define S as the graded polynomial ring with deg(x_i)=w_i
For all choices of homogeneous elements g_1 through g_d in S that form a regular sequence and satisfy deg(g_i)=e_i
Then the graded Hilbert series identity holds for the quotient S modulo the ideal generated by g_1 through g_d

witness_dependencies: The Hilbert series formula uses only the degrees e_i of the given regular sequence elements g_i; it does not depend on any other data about g_i beyond regularity and homogeneity
The grading weights w_i determine the denominator factors 1 minus q to the w_i
Indexing is aligned: g_i has degree e_i for the same i used for w_i
